title: The Bat and the Weasels

full_text:
A little bat, swooping carelessly through the twilight after moths, collided with an oak branch and tumbled into the burrow of a fierce weasel. The weasel seized the bat in her sharp claws, hissing with triumph: "Aha! A bird! I despise all winged creatures that fly in the air and steal eggs from nests; I intend to devour you on the spot!"

The nimble-witted bat squeaked in earnest protest: "A bird? Look closely at me, good madam! What feathers do I possess? I have soft fur, sharp ears, and warm mammalian blood; I am a mouse, a fellow creature of the ground!"

Seeing no feathers, the weasel was convinced and released the bat into the evening air.

A few nights later, the bat tumbled into the den of another weasel who harbored a deadly hatred for all mice and rodents. "At last, a plump mouse for dinner!" snarled the second predator.

"A mouse?" gasped the bat with theatrical horror. "Heaven forbid! Have you ever seen a mouse with leathery wings who can soar among the stars? I am a bird of the night, a winged aeronaut!"

The second weasel marveled at the wings and let him fly away unharmed. Thus, by knowing how to present different aspects of his nature according to the danger at hand, the clever bat saved his life twice in succession.
moral: It is wise to adapt your position to circumstance when survival is at stake.
